## What this compares

The influence-function (IF) PEHE score as written in Alaa & van der Schaar
(2019) is wrong. Their appendix writes PEHE as Ψ¹ + Ψ² + Ψ³ where it should be
Ψ¹ + Ψ² − 2Ψ³, and the three Ψ̇ it lists are not the influence functions of
those Ψ's. Two alternatives are scored here against the scores the study
already reports:

| score | formula | surrogate |
|---|---|---|
| **DR risk** (`dr`) | mean (φ − τ̂)² | – |
| **One-step** (`onestep`) | mean [(τ̃ − τ̂)² + 2(τ̃ − τ̂)(φ − τ̃)] | plug-in τ̃ = μ̂₁ − μ̂₀ (T-learner: the scoring pipeline's per-arm outcome models) |
| **IF, 2019, φ** (`infl`) | `me_metrics.R::calc_infl_score()` | φ, as the study scores it |
| **IF, 2019, plug-in** (`infl_plugin`) | the same | plug-in τ̃ |
| **IF, C&vdS, plug-in** (`cvds_plugin`) | Curth & van der Schaar (2023) appendix | plug-in τ̃ |
| **IF, C&vdS, φ** (`cvds_phi`) | the same | φ |

The one-step score is the correctly derived IF-corrected PEHE. It simplifies
to (φ − τ̂)² − (φ − τ̃)², so **within a run it is the DR risk minus a constant
shared by every candidate**: it picks the same candidate, with the same
Spearman correlation and regret, and differs from DR only in level. Figure 1
should show the two on top of each other; figure 2 is where they separate.

All scores here are from the **CV (`cv_shared`) arm**: the scoring nuisance is
fit on the candidate's own `V − 1` training folds and predicted on its held-out
fold. The estimated-propensity version of every score is in the main
figures; the fixed π = 0.5 version is in the appendix. Every score, and true
PEHE, is a loss: lower is better.

Produced by `me_infl_investigation.R` (`population` and `sims strategies`).

```{r data}
inv_path <- file.path(
  dirname(here()), "results", "correlated", "model_evaluation", "investigation"
)

ARM <- "cv_shared"

check <- readRDS(file.path(inv_path, "me_strat_infl_check.RDS"))
population <- readRDS(file.path(inv_path, "population.RDS"))

scenario_labels <- c(
  `1` = "Null",
  `2` = "Simple",
  `3` = "Complex",
  `4` = "Non-linear"
)

score_labels <- c(
  dr = "DR risk",
  onestep = "One-step",
  infl = "IF, 2019, phi",
  infl_plugin = "IF, 2019, plug-in",
  cvds_plugin = "IF, C&vdS, plug-in",
  cvds_phi = "IF, C&vdS, phi"
)

pipeline_labels <- c(xgb = "XGBoost", automl = "AutoML")

# the score names carry the propensity regime as a trailing "05"
# (cvds_plugin05, onestep05, ...), as me_metrics.R's do
tidy_axes <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    filter(arm == ARM) %>%
    mutate(
      pi_regime = ifelse(grepl("05$", score), "fixed", "estimated"),
      score = factor(
        score_labels[sub("05$", "", score)],
        levels = unname(score_labels)
      ),
      scenario = factor(
        scenario_labels[as.character(scenario)],
        levels = unname(scenario_labels)
      ),
      n = factor(n, levels = sort(unique(n))),
      pipeline = factor(
        pipeline_labels[pipeline],
        levels = unname(pipeline_labels)
      )
    )
}

perf <- tidy_axes(check$perf)
scores <- tidy_axes(check$scores)

# mean +/- Monte Carlo SE over runs, per (scenario, n, pipeline, score, pi)
perf_summary <- perf %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, pipeline, score, pi_regime) %>%
  summarise(
    runs = n(),
    mean_regret = mean(regret),
    mcse_regret = sd(regret) / sqrt(runs),
    mean_rho = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    mcse_rho = sd(spearman, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(spearman))),
    mean_top1 = mean(top1),
    mcse_top1 = sqrt(mean_top1 * (1 - mean_top1) / runs),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# expected regret of ignoring every score and picking a candidate uniformly at
# random - the floor a useful score has to beat
random_baseline <- scores %>%
  distinct(scenario, n, run, model, true_pehe) %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, run) %>%
  summarise(random_regret = mean(true_pehe) - min(true_pehe), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(scenario, n) %>%
  summarise(random_regret = mean(random_regret), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r plot-helpers, include=FALSE}
house_theme <- theme_bw() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

score_colours <- setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe", length(score_labels))),
  unname(score_labels)
)

# One-step is drawn as an open circle in the SAME dodge slot as DR risk, so
# where they coincide - which within a run they always should - the open
# circle rings the filled one instead of looking like a missing series.
is_onestep <- unname(score_labels) == score_labels[["onestep"]]
score_shapes <- setNames(ifelse(is_onestep, 1, 16), unname(score_labels))
score_sizes <- setNames(ifelse(is_onestep, 3.5, 2), unname(score_labels))

dodge_slot <- function(score) {
  ifelse(score == score_labels[["onestep"]], score_labels[["dr"]], as.character(score))
}

selection_plot <- function(df, mean_col, mcse_col, title, ylab,
                           baseline = NULL, hline = NULL, alpha = 0.05) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      est = .data[[mean_col]],
      lo = est - z * .data[[mcse_col]],
      hi = est + z * .data[[mcse_col]],
      slot = dodge_slot(score)
    )
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.6)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = n, y = est, colour = score, group = slot))
  if (!is.null(hline)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = hline, linetype = "dashed")
  }
  if (!is.null(baseline)) {
    p <- p + geom_point(
      data = baseline,
      aes(x = n, y = random_regret),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "grey40"
    )
  }
  p +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
      position = dodge, linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.3
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = score, size = score), position = dodge) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario), cols = vars(pipeline), scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = score_colours) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = score_shapes) +
    scale_size_manual(values = score_sizes) +
    house_theme +
    labs(
      title = title, y = ylab, x = "sample size",
      colour = "Score", shape = "Score", size = "Score"
    )
}

# signed log for the level figure: linear within +/- sigma of zero, log
# beyond, so DR's small positive offset and C&vdS's large negative one are
# both readable on one axis
signed_log <- scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.05, base = 10)

level_plot <- function(df, title) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = score, y = value - true_pehe, colour = score)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "transparent", outlier.shape = NA) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario), cols = vars(n)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = score_colours) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      trans = signed_log,
      breaks = c(-100, -10, -1, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 1, 10, 100)
    ) +
    house_theme +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      y = "score - true PEHE (signed log scale)",
      x = NULL,
      colour = "Score"
    )
}
```

## Checks

```{r runs}
perf %>%
  filter(pi_regime == "estimated") %>%
  distinct(scenario, n, pipeline, score, run) %>%
  count(scenario, n, pipeline, score, name = "runs") %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, pipeline) %>%
  summarise(min_runs = min(runs), max_runs = max(runs), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = pipeline, values_from = c(min_runs, max_runs)) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0(
    "Runs scored per cell (100 expected), ", ARM,
    " arm. Runs with an NA score for any candidate are dropped."
  ))
```

```{r onestep-equals-dr}
# One-step and DR differ by a candidate-independent term within a run, so
# every run should pick the same candidate under both. Anything below 1 is a
# bug in the scoring, not a finding.
perf %>%
  filter(score %in% score_labels[c("dr", "onestep")]) %>%
  select(scenario, n, run, pipeline, pi_regime, score, regret) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = score, values_from = regret) %>%
  group_by(pipeline, pi_regime) %>%
  summarise(
    runs = n(),
    same_pick = mean(abs(.data[[score_labels[["onestep"]]]] -
                           .data[[score_labels[["dr"]]]]) < 1e-10),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Share of runs where One-step and DR risk have the same regret")
```

## 1. Does the score pick a good candidate?

Regret is the true PEHE of the candidate the score picks, minus the true PEHE
of the best of the 9. Points are means over runs with 95% Monte Carlo
intervals; the grey cross is the expected regret of picking a candidate at
random. One-step (open circle) should ring DR risk (filled) exactly.

```{r fig-regret, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_regret", "mcse_regret",
  title = paste0("Regret, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "mean regret (PEHE)",
  baseline = random_baseline
)
```

```{r fig-rho, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_rho", "mcse_rho",
  title = paste0("Spearman correlation with true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "mean Spearman correlation",
  hline = 0
)
```

```{r fig-top1, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_top1", "mcse_top1",
  title = paste0("Top-1 hit rate, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "share of runs picking the true best candidate",
  hline = 1 / 9
)
```

The dashed line on the top-1 figure is 1/9, a random pick.

## 2. Does the score estimate PEHE itself?

Every ranking measure above is blind to a shift shared by all candidates, so
it cannot tell One-step from DR. This can: each candidate's score minus its
true PEHE, over runs. A score that estimates PEHE sits on zero. DR risk should
sit above zero by roughly the variance of φ about τ; One-step should not.

```{r fig-level-xgb, fig.height=9}
level_plot(
  filter(scores, pi_regime == "estimated", pipeline == "XGBoost"),
  paste0("Score minus true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, XGBoost, estimated propensity")
)
```

```{r level-table}
scores %>%
  filter(pi_regime == "estimated") %>%
  group_by(pipeline, score, n) %>%
  summarise(bias = mean(value - true_pehe, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n, values_from = bias, names_prefix = "n = ") %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = paste0(
    "Mean of score minus true PEHE, over scenarios, runs and candidates (",
    ARM, " arm, estimated propensity)"
  ))
```

## 3. Population check: is the formula right before any estimation noise?

From `me_infl_investigation.R population`: N = 2·10⁶ draws per scenario,
**oracle** nuisances (true μ₀, μ₁ and π = 0.5), five constructed candidates
(the truth, the ATE, the truth shrunk halfway to the ATE, μ₁, and τ + X2). With
no nuisance error a correct PEHE estimator lies on the diagonal, and a correct
ranking is at least monotone in true PEHE. The One-step score here uses a
deliberately biased surrogate, τ + 0.3·X2, so its gap from the diagonal is the
second-order remainder the correction leaves behind.

```{r fig-population, fig.height=7}
pop_labels <- c(
  dr = "DR risk",
  onestep_biased_sur = "One-step (biased surrogate)",
  infl_tau = "IF, 2019, true tau",
  infl_phi = "IF, 2019, phi",
  infl_cvds_tau = "IF, C&vdS, true tau",
  infl_cvds_phi = "IF, C&vdS, phi"
)

population %>%
  pivot_longer(
    any_of(names(pop_labels)),
    names_to = "score", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    score = factor(pop_labels[score], levels = unname(pop_labels)),
    scenario = factor(
      scenario_labels[as.character(scenario)],
      levels = unname(scenario_labels)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(scenario, score, true_pehe) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = true_pehe, y = value, colour = score)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  house_theme +
  labs(
    title = "Score against true PEHE, oracle nuisances",
    x = "true PEHE", y = "score", colour = "Score"
  )
```

## 4. Run by run: how often does each score lose to DR risk?

Per run, the score's regret minus DR risk's. Below zero the score picked a
better candidate than DR did; above, a worse one. This separates a score that
is a little worse every run from one that is usually fine and occasionally
picks badly. One-step is left out: it is identically zero.

```{r fig-paired, fig.height=9}
paired <- perf %>%
  filter(pi_regime == "estimated") %>%
  select(scenario, n, run, pipeline, score, regret) %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, run, pipeline) %>%
  filter(any(score == score_labels[["dr"]])) %>%
  mutate(diff = regret - regret[score == score_labels[["dr"]]]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!score %in% score_labels[c("dr", "onestep")])

ggplot(paired, aes(x = score, y = diff, colour = pipeline)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "transparent", outlier.shape = NA) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario), cols = vars(n), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  house_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Regret minus DR risk's regret, per run, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
    y = "regret difference (PEHE)", x = NULL, colour = "Pipeline"
  )
```

```{r paired-table}
paired %>%
  group_by(pipeline, score, n) %>%
  summarise(worse = mean(diff > 1e-10), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n, values_from = worse, names_prefix = "n = ") %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Share of runs where the score picks a worse candidate than DR risk")
```

## Appendix

### Fixed propensity (π = 0.5)

The DGM assigns treatment by a fair coin, so π = 0.5 is the true propensity
and these are oracle-π versions of every score.

```{r fig-regret-fixed, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "fixed"),
  "mean_regret", "mcse_regret",
  title = paste0("Regret, ", ARM, " arm, propensity fixed at 0.5"),
  ylab = "mean regret (PEHE)",
  baseline = random_baseline
)
```

```{r fig-level-fixed, fig.height=9}
level_plot(
  filter(scores, pi_regime == "fixed", pipeline == "XGBoost"),
  paste0("Score minus true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, XGBoost, propensity fixed at 0.5")
)
```

### AutoML pipeline, level

```{r fig-level-automl, fig.height=9}
level_plot(
  filter(scores, pi_regime == "estimated", pipeline == "AutoML"),
  paste0("Score minus true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, AutoML, estimated propensity")
)
```
